exact_quote: All instructions have an optional guard predicate which controls conditional execution of the instruction. The syntax to specify conditional execution is to prefix an instruction with @{!}p, where p is a predicate variable, optionally negated. Instructions without a guard predicate are executed unconditionally.
context_before: PDF page 132: section 9.3 Predicated Execution heading; 'In PTX, predicate registers are virtual and have .pred as the type specifier... .reg .pred p, q, r;'
context_after: PDF page 132: official examples 'setp.lt.s32 p, i, n; // p = (i < n)' / '@p add.s32 j, j, 1; // if i < n, add 1 to j' and 'setp.lt.s32 p, i, n; // compare i to n' / '@!p bra L1; // if False, branch over' / 'add.s32 j, j, 1;'
reason_for_inclusion: PDF rendering of the uniform guard rule (section 9.3): the guard predicate controls conditional execution of the instruction, and instructions without a guard predicate are executed unconditionally. Together with PTX-9.3-ADD-SUP2-006 this explicitly determines the false-guard behavior of the predication construct applied to any instruction including add.u32.
